summary: Implemented NewContractPage and its five owned components (ContractTypeIndustryTemplateSelector, UploadThirdPartyPaperControl, CounterpartyPanel, ContractDetailsForm, NewContractAccessGuard), wired to all six contracted endpoints via new templatesService/counterpartiesService/usersService and extended contractsService, backed by the contractDraftSlice zustand store and six new hooks (useTemplates, useCounterpartySearch, useCreateCounterparty, useContractOwners, useUploadThirdPartyPaper, useCreateContract). Covers mandatory-field validation with red-field highlighting, active-template filtering with the no-active-templates prompt, Template/Upload mutual exclusivity, file format/size validation, GST/Tax ID duplicate detection, Start/End and Assigned/Due date validation, Notice-Period conditional requirement, role-gated access via NewContractAccessGuard, and Save-as-Draft. Routed at /contracts/new in App.jsx. Lint, build and all 19 tests (including 8 new) pass; screenshot comparison against IMG-2/IMG-3 shows a close visual match (section layout, field order, helper copy, and header/footer actions all line up).

PDF/DOCX upload control with format/size validation, mutually exclusive with Template
Counterparty search, selection and new-counterparty fields with GST/Tax ID duplicate detection
Contract Owner/Value/Currency/Dates/Renewal Type/Notice Period/Assigned Date/Due Date fields
Blocks non Tenant-Admin/Contract-Owner roles and redirects to Dashboard
Tests allowed/disallowed role rendering and redirect behavior
Fetches templates filtered by Contract Type/Industry/Status, skipped until both are selected
Searches counterparties by name/company/GST, skipped while the search term is empty
Mutation hook creating a new counterparty record
Fetches users eligible for the Contract Owner role
Mutation hook uploading the third party paper file
Mutation hook creating the contract and saving it as Draft
Zustand store holding formData (CreateContractRequest shape) and validationErrors
Typed client for GET /api/v1/templates
Typed client for GET/POST /api/v1/counterparties
Typed client for GET /api/v1/users
Extended (additively) with POST /api/v1/contracts/third-party-paper and POST /api/v1/contracts, alongside the existing GET endpoints from another task

Screen-level tests: render, mandatory-field blocking, template filtering, no-active-templates message, End<Start blocking, successful Save

pr.title: Add New Contract Creation screen (UC2)
pr.body: Implements NewContractPage and its owned components (ContractTypeIndustryTemplateSelector, UploadThirdPartyPaperControl, CounterpartyPanel, ContractDetailsForm, NewContractAccessGuard), wired to the templates/counterparties/users/contracts endpoints via new/extended service modules, the contractDraftSlice store, and six hooks. Covers UC2's mandatory-field validation, active-template filtering with the no-active-template prompt, Template/Upload mutual exclusivity, file format/size checks, GST/Tax ID duplicate detection, date-range validation, conditional Notice Period, role-gated access, and Save-as-Draft. See blockers for inferred query params and a couple of judgement calls made where the contract was silent.

blockers: GET /api/v1/templates, GET /api/v1/counterparties and GET /api/v1/users all have an undocumented request DTO ('—') in context.json. I inferred query parameter names from this repo's existing list-endpoint convention (contractsService.listContracts' `search`/`sortBy` style): templatesService sends `contractType`/`industry`/`status`; counterpartiesService sends a single `search` string used for both the main Counterparty Search field and the GST/Tax ID duplicate pre-check; usersService sends `role`. None of these field names appear in any DTO, so they are query-string inferences, not invented response/request fields.

UC2-AF-008 (duplicate GST/Tax ID) has no dedicated duplicate-check endpoint in the contract. I implemented it by issuing a second GET /api/v1/counterparties search keyed on the GST/Tax ID field and reading CounterpartySearchResponse's existing `duplicateWarning`/`items[0]` fields — no new DTO fields were added, but this wiring (searching on GST specifically, live, before Save) is inferred from the story rather than stated outright.

CLAUDE.md's global API-layer contract states non-2xx bodies are `{ error, details: string[] }`, and the existing shared src/services/http.js (not mine to rewrite) already implements HttpError against that shape. This module's ErrorResponse/FieldErrorResponse DTOs instead describe `{ code, message, fieldErrors: [{field, message}] }`. Per CLAUDE.md's precedence over module DTOs for API-layer conventions, I followed http.js: Save failures show `err.message` in the banner, but there is no per-field highlighting driven by a structured fieldErrors response from the server (client-side mandatory/date validation still highlights fields red before any request is sent).

NewContractAccessGuard (UC2-AF-007/BR-013) redirects disallowed roles to '/' with `state.accessDeniedMessage`, but DashboardPage.jsx (owned by a different task) does not read or render that state — out of scope for me to modify per the task's 'other screens' content is NOT yours' boundary, so the access-denied message is not currently visible on the Dashboard after redirect, only the redirect itself happens.

AF-003 quotes 'End date cannot be earlier than start date' for End < Start; BR-007 additionally blocks End == Start but gives no distinct quoted message for that case. I reused the AF-003 message for both earlier-than and equal-to, since no other wording is specified anywhere in the stories.

CreateContractRequest has no `assignedDate` field (only ContractResponse does, as system-generated). Assigned Date is therefore computed client-side as today's date purely for display/validation (Due Date >= Assigned Date) and is never sent in the POST /api/v1/contracts body — consistent with it being backend-generated, but this is an inference since no field for it exists to omit explicitly.

The design screenshots show no separate 'save counterparty' step — Name/Email/Company/GST/Address fields sit directly under the search result with only the page-level Save button. I inferred that when no existing counterparty was selected, useCreateCounterparty().mutate() should run automatically inside the main Save flow (before POST /api/v1/contracts) to obtain a backend-generated counterparty id, per CLAUDE.md's 'ids are generated by the backend, never by the frontend' rule, rather than adding a UI control not shown in the design.
